About Me

I’m a Staff Research Scientist at Bosch AI Research Center, enabling AI models to see, understand, and simulate the world around us. My research spans vision foundation models, HD map generation, generative world models, and spatial reasoning for vision-language models. As a technical lead, I also guide model development and collaborate with product teams to bring our research into autonomous driving and manufacturing applications.

Outside of research, I enjoy dancing, playing board games, and spending time with my three cats and one dog!

Industry Experience & Applied Research

Perceive. Understand. Anticipate.

My work spans HD map generation, vision foundation models, and predictive world models, with applications in autonomous driving and manufacturing.

01

Production-scale HD Map Autolabelling

Technical lead for HD map auto-labelling project spanning 10 million driving clips. Lead end-to-end model development, supported by full-time associates, and coordinate with product integration and data production teams to deliver models into production.

The pipeline generates preliminary labels that human labellers refine with minor adjustments, accelerating annotation and reducing manual effort. The production line has contributed to approximately €3 billion in human-labelling cost reductions.

02

Vision Foundation Models for Scene Understandings

Own end-to-end model development for open-vocabulary and in-context segmentation, partnering with product integration teams to deploy vision foundation models in Bosch’s autonomous driving and manufacturing products.

USE enables open-vocabulary data mining for autonomous driving, helping teams identify driving scenes of interest through natural-language queries. ProSAM uses visual examples to automatically label scratches, irregular shapes, and other defects, helping manufacturing plants reduce manual annotation effort. Together, these models bring research advances into production workflows for driving-scene discovery and defect autolabelling.

Mean IoU (%) on open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. COCO† uses all segment–text pairs from COCO images, including annotations from Visual Genome. The COCO + VG variant additionally uses Visual Genome images. CLIP-based two-stage methods use ViT-L/14; the all-methods view includes different architectures.

Designed an auto-labelling pipeline to curate millions of segment-text pairs and trained a vision-language model through contrastive learning to produce universal segment embeddings, enabling zero-shot segmentation and text-based region retrieval. Achieved 37.0% mIoU on ADE20K-150, a 25% relative improvement over OVSeg.

Source: Submitted manuscript · Table 1 · p. 6

500 evaluation clips per dataset. Traffic overlap is the detector-based CR proxy, not a physical collision rate. Overall edited-trajectory results average five maneuvers equally. Agent errors use normalized image coordinates under recorded ego trajectories; ego errors assess adherence to edited trajectories. Values are from the supplied CVPR 2027 submission.

Compared with Cosmos 3, ReactDrive reduced detected traffic-overlap rates by 44.7% on Waymo and 83.0% on nuPlan. Augmenting planner training data with our generated videos improved TransFuser’s NAVSIM planning score (PDMS) from 83.8 to 85.1.

Mean ± standard deviation over 500 generated near-boundary graphs per adjacent class pair. Near-boundary criterion: each target-class probability between 0.45 and 0.55. Designed an adaptive objective to generate graphs near decision boundaries and analyze boundary margin, thickness, and complexity. Achieved up to 3× the success rate of a cross-entropy baseline in generating near-boundary graphs on ENZYMES.
